title: Original IELTS Reading Interface Demonstration
notice: All 40 questions are original simulator demonstration material, not Cambridge or official IELTS questions. Passages are deliberately shorter than IELTS examination passages.

passages.title: Community Gardens and Shared Spaces
paragraphs: Community gardens allow residents to grow vegetables in shared spaces. Volunteers maintain paths, beds and compost bins. Most plots are managed by neighbourhood groups.
Some gardens offer workshops on composting, seed saving and water conservation. Participation is voluntary, and workshops are usually held on Saturdays.
A city survey recorded 120 volunteers in spring and 180 volunteers in autumn. Organisers said that access to tools and reliable water supplies were important for maintaining the gardens.

passages.title: The Changing Role of Public Libraries
paragraphs: Public libraries provide books, quiet study areas and free internet access. Many libraries also lend digital books to registered members.
At the Riverside Library, adult workshops are held on weekends. Children's storytelling sessions take place on Wednesday afternoons. A separate room is available for group study.
Library staff reported that visitors most often asked for help with online forms. The library extended its opening hours on Thursdays but remained closed on Sundays.

passages.title: Safer Cycling in Cities
paragraphs: Protected cycle lanes separate cyclists from motor traffic using barriers or raised kerbs. Several cities have invested in connected routes rather than isolated short sections.
A commuter survey identified safe bicycle parking and predictable journey times as important factors. Respondents also said that poor lighting discouraged evening travel.
A pilot programme added 12 kilometres of protected lanes and installed 300 bicycle parking spaces. Local officials planned to review the programme after two years.
